title.title: Duke's theorem in prime, quartic and sextic degree
title.subtitle: Claim: torus-orbit packets from totally real fields equidistribute, with no escape of mass

object.caption: degree $n$ of the field: known for $2, 3$; claimed for primes $\ge 5$ and primitive $4, 6$

beats.text: Periodic torus orbits in the space of lattices, one packet per totally real field
Duke (1988) did degree 2; Einsiedler, Lindenstrauss, Michel and Venkatesh degree 3
Claimed: every prime degree $\ge 5$, plus primitive quartic and sextic fields

achievement.label: Higher-degree analogues of Duke's theorem
achievement.note: Degrees 4 and 6 need primitive fields; measure rigidity is a black box

verify.detail: In Lean: the prime-degree theorem. The quartic and sextic results are not formalized
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean docs and allowed axioms; we did not build it

sources.quote: Duke (1988) for degree 2 (CM points and closed geodesics). Einsiedler-Lindenstrauss-Michel-Venkatesh (Annals 2011) proved the cubic-field analogue
in every fixed prime degree >= 5 with arbitrary local homothety types; for arbitrary orders in primitive quartic fields; for maximal orders in primitive sextic fields
equidistribute to Haar measure without escape of mass
Primitive (no intermediate field) restriction in degrees 4 and 6 matters
Measure rigidity (Einsiedler-Katok-Lindenstrauss) is a black-box input.
partial formalization: the prime-degree (>= 5) theorem is formalized (DukePrimeDegree, unconditional); quartic and sextic results are not.
only `propext`, `Quot.sound` and `Classical.choice` for every family here

plain: Special lattice shapes from number fields spread evenly over all shapes, like sand settling flat

steps: Known rigidity leaves only a few possible limits
Prime degree rules out the in-between ones
No mass escapes to infinity, so the limit is even

voice.text: Torus orbits from number fields, one packet per field. Degrees two and three were known.
Rigidity leaves few possible limits; prime degree rules out all but the even one.
Claimed: an even spread, nothing lost.
